# core/x509.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from core/x509.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

Reading X.509 certificates (RFC 5280) and checking their
signatures, for the chain a TLS 1.3 server sends.

What is proved: every access is in bounds, nothing leaks, and every span a
certificate holds lies inside the bytes it was read from. What is read: the
signed part, the signature, the issuer and subject names (as the bytes of
their DER, to be compared as bytes), the validity times, the public key
(RSA, ECDSA P-256 or Ed25519), and the extensions basicConstraints,
keyUsage and subjectAltName. A critical extension of any other kind makes
the certificate unreadable, as RFC 5280 requires. The signature algorithms
are sha256WithRSAEncryption, ecdsa-with-SHA256 and Ed25519. Not proved:
that a certificate accepted here is a valid one; the tests check
certificates made by OpenSSL, and that damaged ones, other signers and
other names are refused. Not done: certificate policies, name constraints,
revocation, SHA-384 and SHA-512 signatures and the curve P-384.

`import "core/x509.bastio";` also loads [core/option.bastio](core-option.md), [core/bytes.bastio](core-bytes.md), [core/der.bastio](core-der.md), [core/x25519.bastio](core-x25519.md), [core/endian.bastio](core-endian.md), [core/text.bastio](core-text.md), [core/sha512.bastio](core-sha512.md), [core/ed25519.bastio](core-ed25519.md), [core/sha256.bastio](core-sha256.md), [core/p256.bastio](core-p256.md), [core/rsa.bastio](core-rsa.md).

| Function | |
| --- | --- |
| [`x509_parse`](#x509_parse) | The certificate in `b` (the DER of one `Certificate`, with nothing after it), if it is well formed and of the kinds listed for `X509`. |
| [`x509_signed_by`](#x509_signed_by) | Whether `c`, read from `cb`, was signed by the holder of the key of `issuer`, read from `ib`. |
| [`x509_can_sign`](#x509_can_sign) | Whether `c` may sign certificates. |
| [`x509_valid_at`](#x509_valid_at) | Whether `now` (seconds since 1970) is within the validity of `c`. |
| [`x509_has_name`](#x509_has_name) | Whether `c` has a dNSName in its subjectAltName that matches `name` (case-insensitively; a name like `*.example.org` stands for one label). |

Every example below is built, verified and run by `tests/run.sh`. An `assert` in one is proved at compile time from the contracts above it.

## Types and constants

### `X509`

```bastio
struct X509 {
  tbs: Span, sig_kind: u64, sig: Span, issuer: Span, subject: Span,
  not_before: u64, not_after: u64, key_kind: u64, key_a: Span, key_b: Span,
  key_usage: u64, is_ca: bool, has_san: bool, san: Span
}
```

A certificate read from some bytes. Every span is a range of those bytes.
`tbs` is the signed part including its header; `sig_kind` the signature
algorithm (1 sha256WithRSAEncryption, 2 ecdsa-with-SHA256, 3 Ed25519) and
`sig` the signature; `issuer` and `subject` are the DER of the names;
`not_before` and `not_after` are in seconds since 1970; `key_kind` the key
(1 RSA, 2 ECDSA P-256, 3 Ed25519), for RSA `key_a` the modulus and `key_b`
the exponent, for the others `key_a` the key (65 or 32 bytes). `key_usage`
is the first byte of the keyUsage bits (digitalSignature 128, keyCertSign
4) or 65535 when the extension is missing; `is_ca` is the cA flag of
basicConstraints; `san` the subjectAltName's list of names, if `has_san`.

### `X509Key`

```bastio
struct X509Key { kind: u64, a: Span, b: Span }
```

Internal: a public key: `kind` as in `X509` (0 when unreadable), and the
spans `a` and `b`.

### `X509Exts`

```bastio
struct X509Exts { ok: bool, key_usage: u64, is_ca: bool, has_san: bool, san: Span }
```

Internal: what the extensions of a certificate say.

## Functions

### `x509_parse`

```bastio
fn x509_parse(b: &Bytes) -> Option[X509]
  requires blen(b) < 274877906944
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> result.Some.tbs.start <= result.Some.tbs.end && result.Some.tbs.end <= blen(b)
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> result.Some.sig.start <= result.Some.sig.end && result.Some.sig.end <= blen(b)
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> result.Some.issuer.start <= result.Some.issuer.end && result.Some.issuer.end <= blen(b)
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> result.Some.subject.start <= result.Some.subject.end && result.Some.subject.end <= blen(b)
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> result.Some.key_a.start <= result.Some.key_a.end && result.Some.key_a.end <= blen(b)
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> result.Some.key_b.start <= result.Some.key_b.end && result.Some.key_b.end <= blen(b)
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> result.Some.san.start <= result.Some.san.end && result.Some.san.end <= blen(b)
```

The certificate in `b` (the DER of one `Certificate`, with nothing after
it), if it is well formed and of the kinds listed for `X509`: version 3
(or 1 without extensions), the signature algorithm the same in both
places, the times readable, the key readable and the extensions readable.

Example:

```bastio
let b = bfrom("not a certificate");
let mut bad = 1;
match x509_parse(b) {
  Option::Some(c) => {},
  Option::None => { bad = 0; },
}
bfree(b);
if bad != 0 { return 1; }
```

### `x509_signed_by`

```bastio
fn x509_signed_by(cb: &Bytes, c: X509, ib: &Bytes, issuer: X509) -> bool
  requires span_in(c.tbs, cb) && span_in(c.sig, cb) && span_in(c.issuer, cb)
  requires span_in(issuer.subject, ib) && span_in(issuer.key_a, ib) && span_in(issuer.key_b, ib)
  requires blen(cb) < 274877906944 && blen(ib) < 274877906944
```

Whether `c`, read from `cb`, was signed by the holder of the key of
`issuer`, read from `ib`: the signature algorithm and the key must agree,
the issuer name of `c` must be the subject name of `issuer` byte for byte,
and the signature over the signed part of `c` must verify. Whether
`issuer` may sign certificates is for `x509_can_sign` to say.

Example:

```bastio
let b = bfrom("not a certificate");
let mut ok = true;
match x509_parse(b) {
  Option::Some(c) => { ok = x509_signed_by(b, c, b, c); },
  Option::None => { ok = false; },
}
bfree(b);
if ok { return 1; }
```

### `x509_can_sign`

```bastio
fn x509_can_sign(c: X509) -> bool
```

Whether `c` may sign certificates: its cA flag is set and, if it has a
keyUsage, that includes keyCertSign.

Example:

```bastio
let b = bfrom("not a certificate");
let mut ok = true;
match x509_parse(b) {
  Option::Some(c) => { ok = x509_can_sign(c); },
  Option::None => { ok = false; },
}
bfree(b);
if ok { return 1; }
```

### `x509_valid_at`

```bastio
fn x509_valid_at(c: X509, now: u64) -> bool
```

Whether `now` (seconds since 1970) is within the validity of `c`.

Example:

```bastio
let b = bfrom("not a certificate");
let mut ok = true;
match x509_parse(b) {
  Option::Some(c) => { ok = x509_valid_at(c, 1800000000); },
  Option::None => { ok = false; },
}
bfree(b);
if ok { return 1; }
```

### `x509_has_name`

```bastio
fn x509_has_name(b: &Bytes, c: X509, name: &Bytes) -> bool
  requires span_in(c.san, b)
```

Whether `c` has a dNSName in its subjectAltName that matches `name`
(case-insensitively; a name like `*.example.org` stands for one label).

Example:

```bastio
let b = bfrom("not a certificate");
let name = bfrom("example.org");
let mut ok = true;
match x509_parse(b) {
  Option::Some(c) => { ok = x509_has_name(b, c, name); },
  Option::None => { ok = false; },
}
bfree(name);
bfree(b);
if ok { return 1; }
```

## Internals

### `x509_item`

```bastio
fn x509_item(b: &Bytes, at: u64, limit: u64) -> DerItem
  requires limit <= blen(b) && at <= limit
  ensures result.content.start <= result.content.end && result.content.end <= limit && at <= result.content.start
  ensures result.tag != 0 ==> at + 2 <= result.content.start
```

Internal: the element at `at` before `limit`, or one with the tag 0 and
an empty content at `at` when there is none.

### `x509_nib`

```bastio
fn x509_nib(c: u8) -> u8
  ensures result < 16
```

Internal: the value of the hex digit `c` (0 for anything else).

### `x509_is`

```bastio
fn x509_is(b: &Bytes, it: DerItem, hex: Str) -> bool
  requires it.content.end <= blen(b) && it.content.start <= it.content.end && slen(hex) < 1000
```

Internal: whether the content of `it` is the bytes written as hex in `hex`.

### `x509_same`

```bastio
fn x509_same(b: &Bytes, s1: Span, s2: Span) -> bool
  requires s1.start <= s1.end && s1.end <= blen(b) && s2.start <= s2.end && s2.end <= blen(b)
```

Internal: whether `b[s1.start..s1.end]` and `b[s2.start..s2.end]` are the same bytes.

### `x509_days`

```bastio
fn x509_days(y: u64, m: u64, d: u64) -> u64
  requires y >= 1970 && y <= 9999 && m >= 1 && m <= 12 && d >= 1 && d <= 31
  ensures result < 3000000
```

Internal: the days from 1970-01-01 to the civil date, for years 1970 to
9999 (Howard Hinnant's algorithm).

### `x509_digits`

```bastio
fn x509_digits(b: &Bytes, at: u64, n: u64) -> u64
  requires at + n <= blen(b) && n <= 4
  ensures result < 10000 || result == 99999
```

Internal: the digits `b[at..at+n]` as a number, or 99999 for anything else.

### `x509_time`

```bastio
fn x509_time(b: &Bytes, it: DerItem) -> u64
  requires it.content.end <= blen(b) && it.content.start <= it.content.end
  ensures result < 300000000000
```

Internal: a UTCTime (tag 23) or GeneralizedTime (tag 24) in the form
`...Z` as seconds since 1970, or 0 for anything else (before 1970, an
impossible date, no `Z`, fractions or an offset).

### `x509_sig_kind`

```bastio
fn x509_sig_kind(b: &Bytes, alg: Span) -> u64
  requires alg.start <= alg.end && alg.end <= blen(b)
```

Internal: the signature algorithm in the AlgorithmIdentifier whose
content is `alg` (see `X509`), or 0.

### `x509_no_key`

```bastio
fn x509_no_key() -> X509Key
  ensures result.a.start <= result.a.end && result.a.end == 0 && result.b.start <= result.b.end && result.b.end == 0
```

Internal: the unreadable key.

### `x509_key`

```bastio
fn x509_key(b: &Bytes, spki: Span) -> X509Key
  requires spki.start <= spki.end && spki.end <= blen(b)
  ensures result.a.start <= result.a.end && result.a.end <= spki.end
  ensures result.b.start <= result.b.end && result.b.end <= spki.end
```

Internal: the SubjectPublicKeyInfo whose content is `spki`.

### `x509_exts`

```bastio
fn x509_exts(b: &Bytes, ext: Span) -> X509Exts
  requires ext.start <= ext.end && ext.end <= blen(b)
  ensures result.san.start <= result.san.end && result.san.end <= ext.end
```

Internal: the Extensions SEQUENCE whose content is `ext`.

### `x509_lower`

```bastio
fn x509_lower(c: u8) -> u8
```

Internal: `c` in lower case.

### `x509_name_match`

```bastio
fn x509_name_match(b: &Bytes, p: Span, name: &Bytes) -> bool
  requires p.start <= p.end && p.end <= blen(b)
```

Internal: whether the DNS name pattern `b[p.start..p.end]` matches `name`:
a case-insensitive match, where a pattern may start with `*.` to stand for
exactly one label of the name (and only if at least two labels follow it).
